summary.headline: Can Fin Homes Q1 FY27 disbursements rose 29% YoY to INR 2,609 crores, but rundown of INR 1,857 crores absorbed the AUM gain.
summary.overview: Disbursements of INR 2,609 crores beat the INR 2,500 crore internal plan and grew 29% YoY across all six zones. Book rundown rose to INR 1,857 crores (from INR 1,730 crores in Q4), mainly from part-prepayments of INR 1,072 crores after the annual-to-quarterly reset, so net AUM growth was about 10.8% YoY. Yield held at 9.81% and cost of borrowing fell to 6.98%, lifting spread to 2.83% and NIM to 3.81%. Management reaffirmed 14% AUM growth and a 10 bps credit cost for FY27, while ROA slipped to 2.39% on higher opex and an IT project rollout is underway across 250 branches.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursement target INR 13,000 crores with 14% AUM growth; management may push to INR 13,200-13,400 crores if needed to offset higher rundown.
Q2 FY27 disbursement target INR 3,000 crores; quarterly path then steps up to INR 3,500 crores and INR 4,000 crores in Q3 and Q4 per prior plan.
NIM to be maintained at 3.81% plus; Q2 incremental bank borrowing at 7.25-7.5% expected to add only marginal cost, on new loans only.
Credit cost guided at 10 bps for FY27; management sees no challenge to this.
Cost-to-income ratio around 19.5% for FY27, trending back toward 18% over about three years.
Remaining 245 branches to move to new IT platform by end of Q2, in tranches at month-end (July, August, September); update expected around September.
Opex: about INR 40 crores of further IT-related costs yet to come; no other major surprises expected.
capex_capacity: New LOS/LMS/report-generation platform live in 5 pilot branches from 8 July 2026, with sanctions, disbursements, NACH, BBPS collections and closures processed.
Rollout to remaining 245 branches (250 total) planned within Q2 FY27, migrating month-end data in tranches.
Management expects about six months for new branches to stabilise on the new system; staffing benefits expected this year with sales additions from existing headcount.
APF (apartment finance) approvals up to 331 projects; per-project exposure capped at 10% of the book per project.
demand_pricing: No demand slowdown seen across geographies; partner banks willing to sanction, including a couple of large sanctions.
Bank borrowing rates for new loans now 7.25-7.5% vs about 6.95% last year; existing loans unchanged.
Special-rate threshold raised from INR 20 lakh to INR 25 lakh loans, to offset higher incremental borrowing costs.
Customer pricing range about 8.4% (best, salaried, CIBIL above 725, INR 25 lakh+) to about 12.5% (non-salaried, non-housing, S3); blended yield 9.81%.
Competition: LIC and Bajaj Housing are the main rivals in branches; Bajaj growing around 25-30% per analyst comment, with its technology edge cited.
Best rate gap to banks widened from 55 bps to over 100 bps after repo cuts; management says it cannot close the gap cheaply.
82% of loans now have CIBIL score above 700 (vs about 75% earlier); 80% of business sourced via DSA.

qa_highlights.question: Macro, underwriting and asset quality outlook for next 3-6 months, and any changes to norms or customer filters (salaried vs self-employed rejections)?
qa_highlights.answer: No demand slowdown across geographies; 60 APF projects added in Q1 (271 to 331 approved). Rates for new bank loans are 7.25-7.5% vs 6.95% last year. Special-rate threshold moved from INR 20 lakh to INR 25 lakh, customer re-rating parameters and EWS/OTMS monitoring added, and 82% of loans now have CIBIL above 700 (vs about 75% earlier). Expect some indirect rise in rejection ratios; 80% of business comes via DSA.

qa_highlights.question: Status of IT rollout (LOS, LMS, report generation) and any impact on disbursement targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Pilot in 5 branches went live on 8 July 2026 using 30 June data, processing sanctions, disbursements, NACH, BBPS and closures with only minor teething issues. Remaining 245 branches to move in month-end tranches (July, August, September), with a further update around September; INR 3,000 crore Q2 target unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Pricing and blended yield by segment; are there trade-offs by ticket size?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended yield 9.81% (9.82% last year). Best rate about 8.4% for salaried, CIBIL above 725, loans of INR 25 lakh plus; highest about 12.5% for non-salaried, non-housing, S3 customers.

qa_highlights.question: Housing vs non-housing and salaried vs self-employed growth; number of loans; run-rate going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Housing disbursements INR 1,650 crore (+28% YoY) and LAP INR 958 crore (+32%); salaried +21%, SENP +44%. Management gave amounts only, not loan account counts. FY27 disbursement target INR 13,000 crore unchanged, with a possible push to INR 13,200-13,400 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the IT-sector hiring slowdown in Bangalore affecting home loan offtake or policy?
qa_highlights.answer: No major impact seen so far: Karnataka grew 18% YoY and Telangana slightly more (partly base effect). IT-sector customers are about 6% of the base, with top IT employers barely represented. Karnataka NPA was lower in absolute terms at March 2026 vs March 2025, with only a marginal June increase.

qa_highlights.question: Any opex surprises in FY27 and how far is APF exposure per project capped?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 40 crore of further IT-related cost to come, with AMCs and depreciation starting; salary, rent and other costs in line with last year. Cost-to-income about 19.5% for FY27, trending toward 18% in about three years. APF exposure capped at 10% of the book per project.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the book rundown elevated for four quarters, and is the 4% level the new normal? Also, how does the best-rate gap to banks affect pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Part-prepayments of INR 1,072 crore (vs INR 976 crore) drove the rundown, as borrowers under change-in-tenure kept EMIs constant and paid down principal. BT-outs were INR 408 crore (vs INR 400 crore), and other closures INR 377 crore (vs INR 360 crore). Best rate gap widened from 55 bps to over 100 bps; management is exploring deposit conversion and bureau alerts for retention.

qa_highlights.question: Can ROA of about 2.4% and ROE of about 18% be achieved in FY27 given higher opex and the soft Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 ROA was 2.39% (2.53% last year) and ROE 18%+. Management said the cost impact is already visible and expects to manage ROA, with NIM and spread on track and credit cost not a concern. Q1 NPA rise was only INR 17-18 crore vs INR 45 crore last Q1 FY26.

risks_watch: Book rundown: part-prepayments of INR 1,857 crore in Q1 (INR 1,072 crore part-prepay) mean FY27 disbursements may need to exceed INR 13,000 crore to hold 14% AUM growth; Q2 target is INR 3,000 crore.

IT rollout: 245 remaining branches migrate in month-end tranches through September; update expected around September. Management noted 50-100 branches will need more handholding than the 5-branch pilot.
Cost of funds: new bank loans priced at 7.25-7.5% vs 6.95% last year; NIM guidance of 3.81%+ depends on incremental-only pass-through and yield mix shift.
Competitive pricing gap: best rate spread to banks/larger players widened to over 100 bps from 55 bps; LIC and Bajaj Housing (growing about 25-30% per analyst) are main rivals.
Asset quality: SENP current NPA about 1.45-1.5% vs about 0.6-0.63% for salaried; IT-sector and Karnataka exposure monitored with early-warning signals; credit cost guided at 10 bps.
Opex: cost-to-income moved from about 18% to 19%+ in Q1, FY27 guided near 19.5%; about INR 40 crore of further IT costs yet to come.
key_quotes: So against INR 2,500 crores, which was what was planned and what was projected, we have achieved INR2,609 crores.
So, we are confident that the NIM will be maintained at 3.81% plus and we should not have a problem in that.
And so the 10 bps that we have been talking about, definitely doesn't look to be a challenge this year.

The major challenge or the major portion from where our run down is happening is actually amortization and more importantly, part prepayment where customers are making more payments every month, and but the loans are still with us.
summary.management_tone: Confident on disbursements, asset quality and the 14% AUM growth target, but cautious on the higher book rundown, the widened pricing gap to banks and the IT rollout's business impact. Management was candid about the rundown and competitive pressures, and it deferred on new product launches, saying the Board has not yet deliberated.
